items.label: A
items.critique: Over-the-top opener ('What took you so long to get here!?'), stock 'reward you handsomely', a plain item handoff and a bare journal with a number in it ('Rescue the 6 trapped mine workers'): Westwood's functional, slightly clumsy plainness.

items.label: B
items.critique: Cosy hamlet texture ('net-man', 'old mill steps', 'Oh my, oh my...') and a captive who seeds the next quest with a stammered clue: well made, but too crafted and too local-colourful for Nox's blunt quest lines.

items.label: C
items.critique: Tidy cause-and-effect exposition (raid, paddocks, western hills, barred storeroom, back way, food in the crate) and a captive who explains his whole survival; the closing 'makings of a true soldier' is a neat bow Westwood rarely ties.

items.label: D
items.critique: The absurd stakes (a pet frog), the oddly cross captive line 'Fine! I will follow you!' and the deadpan 'Loads and loads of money?' joke are exactly Nox's goofy humour; short, exclaimed, plain.

items.label: E
items.critique: Every line is a small, balanced exclamation with a cute character detail (no stick to fight with, can't ring the chapel bell without him); the even, complete dramatic beats and the double-name journal read as a careful imitation.

items.label: F
items.critique: Bare, almost perfunctory lines ('Help us!', 'Time is running out. Now be on your way!'), 'lovely women' and 'damsels' with period-game cheek, and a quest that just points to the next two groups: unpolished in Westwood's way.

items.label: G
items.critique: Overwrought plot exposition with awkward syntax ('leaving rebuilding the village our smallest concern', 'At happier other times'), 'Damn!' and the cliché 'Time waits for no man!': Westwood's main-plot voice, clumsy but authentic.

items.label: H
items.critique: Close to Nox in its plainness and short captive lines, but the reminder stacks four exclamations in a row and the reward (guards will let you cross) is a tidy mechanical payoff; the journal is cleanly formatted rather than terse.

tells: Westwood's rescue lines are often perfunctory or oddly toned (a captive who sounds annoyed, a one-word 'Help us!'); the new texts give every captive a vivid, explanatory, emotionally fitting speech.
Westwood leans on clumsy syntax and stock phrases ('reward you handsomely', 'Time waits for no man', 'At happier other times'); the new texts are grammatically smooth and evenly paced.

The new texts add local colour and small cute character details (net-man, chapel bell, mill steps, food in the crate) and plant follow-up hooks neatly; Westwood's details are sparse and its humour is broad and absurd (a pet frog, 'Loads and loads of money?').
Westwood journals are bare objectives, sometimes with numerals or 'Charm or kill'; the new journals are uniformly shaped 'Find X in Y and bring him home' sentences.
New reminders tend to stack several short exclamations of urgency; Westwood reminders are a single plain instruction.
